{{short description|Mathematics term}}
{{Expand French|date=June 2021}}

In mathematics and computer science, a '''morphic word''' or '''substitutive word''' is an infinite sequence of symbols which is constructed from a particular class of [[endomorphism]] of a [[free monoid]].

Every [[automatic sequence]] is morphic.<ref name=LotIII524/>

==Definition==
Let ''f'' be an endomorphism of the free monoid ''A''<sup>&lowast;</sup> on an alphabet ''A'' with the property that there is a letter ''a'' such that ''f''(''a'') = ''as'' for a non-empty string ''s'': we say that ''f'' is '''prolongable''' at ''a''.  The word

:<math> a s f(s) f(f(s)) \cdots f^{(n)}(s) \cdots \ </math>

is a '''pure morphic''' or '''pure substitutive word'''.  Note that it is the limit of the sequence ''a'', ''f''(''a''), ''f''(''f''(''a'')), ''f''(''f''(''f''(''a''))), ...
It is clearly a fixed point of the endomorphism ''f'': the unique such sequence beginning with the letter ''a''.<ref name=LotII10>Lothaire (2011) p.&nbsp;10</ref><ref name=Hon505>Honkala (2010) p.505</ref> In general, a morphic word is the image of a pure morphic word under a coding, that is, a morphism that maps letter to letter.<ref name=LotIII524/>

If a morphic word is constructed as the fixed point of a prolongable ''k''-[[uniform morphism]] on ''A''<sup>&lowast;</sup> then the word is ''k''-[[automatic sequence|automatic]].  The ''n''-th term in such a sequence can be produced by a [[finite-state automaton]] reading the digits of ''n'' in base ''k''.<ref name=LotIII524/>

==Examples==
* The [[Thue–Morse sequence]] is generated over {0,1} by the 2-uniform endomorphism 0 → 01, 1 → 10.<ref name=LotII11>Lothaire (2011) p.&nbsp;11</ref><ref name=LotIII525>Lothaire (2005) p.525</ref>
* The [[Fibonacci word]]  is generated over {''a'',''b''} by the endomorphism ''a'' → ''ab'', ''b'' → ''a''.<ref name=LotIII524>Lothaire (2005) p.524</ref><ref name=LotII11/>
* The [[tribonacci word]] is generated over {''a'',''b'',''c''} by the endomorphism ''a'' → ''ab'', ''b'' → ''ac'', ''c'' → ''a''.<ref name=LotIII525/>
* The [[Rudin–Shapiro sequence]] is obtained from the fixed point of the 2-uniform morphism ''a'' → ''ab'', ''b'' → ''ac'', ''c'' → ''db'', ''d'' → ''dc''  followed by the coding ''a'',''b'' → 0, ''c'',''d'' → 1.<ref name=LotIII525/>
* The [[regular paperfolding sequence]] is obtained from the fixed point of the 2-uniform morphism ''a'' → ''ab'', ''b'' → ''cb'', ''c'' → ''ad'', ''d'' → ''cd''  followed by the coding ''a'',''b'' → 0, ''c'',''d'' → 1.<ref name=LotIII526>Lothaire (2005) p.526</ref>

==D0L system==
A '''D0L system''' (deterministic context-free [[Lindenmayer system]]) is given by a word ''w'' of the free monoid ''A''<sup>&lowast;</sup> on an alphabet ''A'' together with a morphism σ prolongable at ''w''.  The system generates the infinite D0L word ω = lim<sub>''n''→∞</sub> σ<sup>''n''</sup>(''w'').  Purely morphic words are D0L words but not conversely.  However, if ω = ''u''ν is an infinite D0L word with an initial segment ''u'' of length |''u''| ≥ |''w''|, then ''z''ν is a purely morphic word, where ''z'' is a letter not in ''A''.<ref name=Hon506>Honkala (2010) p.506</ref>
